transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. I came in because I've been having these big eating spells, and afterward, I just feel disgusted with myself and very guilty about what I've done. It has been very hard to carry this secret around, and I just feel so ashamed.
After these eating spells, do you ever try to prevent weight gain by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of those things like making myself throw up, taking laxatives, or exercising to stop from gaining weight. Usually, I just sit there at the kitchen table feeling absolutely terrible and guilty about what I've done.
Do you worry a lot about your weight or body shape, or do these eating spells happen mainly when you are stressed or upset rather than because of weight concerns?

No, it's not really about my weight or how I look at my age. It's just that I've been feeling so deeply stressed, overwhelmed, and lonely caring for my husband and worrying about his failing health. When the house is quiet and I'm all alone with my worries, that's when I seem to turn to the food.
When these eating spells happen, do you feel a strong fear of gaining weight or a preoccupation with your body shape, or is it mainly a response to stress and loneliness?

It really isn't about a fear of gaining weight or how my body looks at all. It is entirely a response to the stress and isolation of caring for my husband, and I just turn to food for comfort late at night when I'm feeling overwhelmed.
Do the eating episodes happen mainly as a response to stress, loneliness, or other emotional distress, or do they occur even when you are not upset and feel more like a loss of control over eating?

It is really a mix of both, doctor. The urge to start eating usually comes when I am feeling so lonely and stressed about my husband's health late at night. But once I actually begin, a complete loss of control takes over and I feel like I just can't hit the brakes, even when I am telling myself to stop.
Do you ever eat large amounts of food and then intentionally try to get rid of it or compensate afterward, such as by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising?

No, doctor, I don't do any of those things to get rid of the food afterward. I've never tried to make myself throw up, take laxatives, or fast to make up for it. I just sit there with the heavy feeling in my stomach and the guilt.
When you have these eating spells, do they mainly happen only during times of stress or loneliness, or do they also happen at other times when you are not feeling upset?

I'm not entirely sure, but they mostly seem to happen late at night when I am feeling lonely, worried about my husband, or overwhelmed. I haven't really noticed them happening when I am feeling relaxed or happy.
Do the eating spells happen only when you are feeling stressed, lonely, or upset, and not at other times when your mood is okay?

Yes, doctor, they almost always happen late at night when I am alone with my worries and feeling overwhelmed by my husband's health. I use food as a comfort during those stressful, lonely moments, and it doesn't really happen when my mood is okay or when I am busy during the day.
Do these eating episodes only happen when you are feeling stressed, lonely, or upset, or do they also happen at times when your mood is otherwise okay and you are not emotionally distressed?

Yes, they really only happen when I am feeling stressed, worried, or lonely. I find myself using the food as a familiar comfort late at night when my husband is asleep and I am left all alone with my worries about his health.
Do you ever have these eating episodes when you are not feeling stressed, lonely, or upset, or do they only happen during those emotional moments?

I haven't really thought about it in those terms, but it seems these episodes almost always happen late at night when I am alone and feeling overwhelmed by my caregiving duties and worried about my husband. They don't really happen when I'm feeling relaxed or happy.
Do these eating episodes happen only during times of stress, loneliness, or other emotional distress, or do they also happen when you feel calm and not upset?

They really only happen when I am feeling stressed and isolated with my worries about my husband's health late at night. I don't have these spells when I am feeling calm or happy. It is strictly a comfort for those overwhelmed, lonely moments.
When you have these eating spells, do they happen only during times when you feel stressed, lonely, or upset, or do they also happen when you feel calm and not distressed?

Yes, they almost always happen when I am feeling stressed, lonely, or worried, rather than when I am calm. They usually occur late at night when my husband is asleep and I am alone with my anxieties about his health. During those quiet, isolating moments, I end up using the food as a source of comfort.
During these eating episodes, do you feel like you eat a clearly large amount of food in a short time, with a strong loss of control, even when you are not physically hungry?

Yes, even if I'm not hungry, I'll eat a massive amount of food all by myself, like a whole big pot of rice and stew that would normally feed my entire family. I eat so quickly, almost like I'm racing, and I feel an absolute loss of control where I tell myself to stop but my hands just keep scooping more and I can't hit the brakes.
Do these eating episodes happen at least once a week for the past 3 months, or are they less frequent than that?

Yes, they've been happening at least once, and usually a couple of times, every single week. This pattern has been going on for about the last three months, ever since my husband's health took a turn and he first went into the hospital.
Have these eating episodes been happening for at least 3 months, with at least one episode per week on average?

Yes, doctor, they have been happening at least once or twice a week for about three months now. This whole pattern started back in the spring when my husband was first hospitalized and his health really took a turn.
Do you ever feel strongly afraid of gaining weight or very concerned about your body shape or size, even outside these eating episodes?

No, I don't really worry much about my weight or my body shape in that way. My main distress and shame are about the eating behavior itself, the complete loss of control, and the terrible guilt that follows afterward. It's not about a fear of gaining weight at all.
Have you ever had a period of time when you regularly ate large amounts of food and then tried to compensate by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

No, I have never done any of those things, like making myself throw up, taking laxatives, fasting, or exercising to make up for the food. I just sit there at the kitchen table afterward, feeling so guilty and ashamed of what I've done.
Do you ever intentionally try to prevent weight gain after these episodes, such as by fasting, skipping meals, vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?
No, I don't do any of those things to prevent weight gain. Usually, I just feel too sluggish and ashamed to do much of anything afterward.

During these episodes, do you feel a true loss of control and eat a clearly large amount of food in a short time, or is it more like eating extra food when you are stressed or lonely but without that loss of control?

It is definitely a true loss of control and a massive amount of food, not just eating a little extra. Once I start, I tell myself 'Maria, stop,' but I just can't hit the brakes and my hands keep scooping more onto my plate. I end up eating what my whole family would normally finish in one Sunday dinner, all by myself in one evening.
Do these eating episodes happen even when you are not feeling stressed, lonely, or upset, or do they only occur during those emotional moments?

I am not quite sure because I have been feeling stressed, worried, or lonely almost constantly since my husband's health declined. Because of that, it is very hard for me to separate those feelings from the eating episodes.
Do your eating episodes also happen at times when you feel calm and not stressed or lonely, or do they only occur when you are upset or overwhelmed?

They really only happen when I am feeling deeply stressed, worried, and isolated. They typically occur late at night when I am alone with my thoughts after a hard day of caregiving, using food as a comfort rather than when I am feeling calm or happy.
Do you have these eating episodes only when you are feeling stressed, lonely, or upset, or do they also happen at times when you feel calm and not emotionally distressed?

These eating episodes almost always happen when I am feeling stressed, worried about my husband, or lonely late at night. I don't really experience them when I am feeling calm or relaxed, as the eating is tied to seeking comfort from the worry and isolation of caregiving.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent binge-eating episodes with objectively large amounts of food, marked loss of control, and significant guilt/disgust afterward. Episodes occur at least 1–2 times weekly for about 3 months. She denies compensatory behaviors and denies weight/shape overvaluation or fear of weight gain. The episodes are strongly linked to stress and loneliness from caregiving, making F50.8 the best fit among the provided options.
